annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held, 'Sharpened up and (8)', is cut short after 'and': 'Sharpened' defines the answer but the rest of the clue is missing, and no scan or search gives it.

parts.note: to name or call something is to term it
the Roman numeral for one is I

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the word for star is read from the bottom up

parts.note: the sun is our star

explanation.surface: A rising star's ambition gets a name.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'rising' reads SUN upwards as NUS; 'star' sounds like a celebrity but is the sun.
explanation.definitionFit: A terminus is an end point or final destination, the place a journey aims at.

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word go

parts.note: Lent is the Christian season of fasting

explanation.surface: Someone finally sets off at speed, humming a tune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'humming' looks like singing, but in British slang it means smelling strongly, and OLENT is an old word for scented.
explanation.definitionFit: Olent means giving off an odour, and humming is British slang for smelly.

parts.note: a put-up job is a fraud or lie, but read literally it is a job of putting up a building simply from ready-made parts

explanation.surface: Something is plainly a set-up, a fraud arranged in advance.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer covers both readings: the second half of the word is a lie, and the whole is factory-made building.
explanation.definitionFit: Assembling buildings from ready-made sections is quick erection, while a fabrication is an invented story, the sense of a put-up job.

indicators.note: knocked up suggests something hastily thrown together, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for one hundred

explanation.surface: A darts player boasts of a powerful throw scoring a hundred.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked up' rearranges DARTS as DRAST; I and C follow. The colon is just punctuation in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Drastic measures are severe or forceful ones, so strong in the sense of extreme.

explanation.surface: A young dandy has struck it rich.
explanation.definitionFit: A buck is an old word for a dashing young man about town, and also American slang for a dollar.

clue.text: Bachelor clears up weed in part of car

parts.note: to rake is to clear up leaves and debris
to hoe is to weed

explanation.surface: A single man tidies the garden and digs out weeds in part of the car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'weed' is a verb here, giving HOE, not a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: The curved block pressed against a wheel drum to slow a vehicle is a component of its braking system.

clue.text: All the players — or the star?

parts.note: the cast is the full set of actors in a production

explanation.surface: A theatre question: does the whole company matter, or just the lead?
explanation.walkthrough: 'the star' reads as the lead actor, but it is a real star, one of the two bright ones in Gemini.
explanation.definitionFit: Castor is one of the twin stars of the Gemini constellation.

clue.text: Renovating in street meant incorporating new diversions

indicators.note: incorporating means taking in, so one letter goes inside the rearranged letters
renovating means remaking, so the letters of the words are rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: Doing up a street meant fitting in fresh amusements.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Renovating' reorders IN STREET MEANT, and 'incorporating' puts N among those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Shows, games and other amusements are entertainments, things that divert people.

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', linking definition to wordplay

indicators.note: mainly means most of a word, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: verdant means green

indicators.note: round means turned about, so the letters for city are read backwards

parts.note: EC is the postcode for the City of London

explanation.surface: A nation is mostly green around one of its towns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mainly' drops the last letter of GREEN; 'round' turns EC (the City of London postcode) back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: Greece is a nation in south-east Europe.

indicators.note: outside means one word wraps round the letter for first-class

parts.note: to annul is to cancel
A, as in A1, means first-class

explanation.surface: A question about top-quality books, followed by a note about cancelled orders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Books' looks like a verb but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Annuals are yearly books, such as children's gift volumes published each Christmas.

indicators.note: by means next to, so the word for property follows the others

parts.note: a trait is a property or characteristic

explanation.surface: A distracted girl sits by her property.
explanation.definitionFit: Distrait means absent-minded and preoccupied, a borrowing from French.

clue.text: Plane's tail with new swept-back movable wing section

indicators.note: tail means the final letter of the word Plane's, without its apostrophe s
swept-back, like a jet's wings, means the word for new is read backwards

parts.note: novel means new

explanation.surface: An aircraft's tail with a new swept-back moving part of the wing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tail' takes E from Plane; 'swept-back' turns NOVEL into LEVON.
explanation.definitionFit: An elevon is an aircraft control surface acting as both elevator and aileron, hinged on a delta wing.

clue.text: Sweet drink added to excessive flattery

indicators.note: added to means the drink comes after the word for excessive flattery

parts.note: to butter someone up is to flatter them excessively
Scotch is whisky

explanation.surface: A sweet drink served with heavy praise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sweet' reads as an adjective describing the drink, but it is the noun definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Butterscotch is a hard brittle confection made from butter and brown sugar.

clue.text: Aggressive culture at odds with New Testament

indicators.note: with means the abbreviation is placed alongside
at odds means out of order, so the letters of culture are jumbled

explanation.surface: A belligerent culture clashes with Christian scripture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at odds' jumbles the letters of culture into the first seven letters, so the anagram is not mixed with the abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Truculent describes someone eager to fight or argue, defiantly hostile.

indicators.note: used in means the abbreviation is placed within the word for roofing

parts.note: tiles are roofing

explanation.surface: Building supplies for the roof of a home extension.
explanation.walkthrough: 'used in' puts the abbreviation inside; 'roofing' looks like an activity but is the material on a roof.
explanation.definitionFit: Textiles are woven fabrics, cloth materials.

explanation.surface: Someone is overlooked because they act on a whim.
explanation.definitionFit: Unconsidered means disregarded, and also done without thought, rash.

explanation.surface: A question about children who steal.
explanation.definitionFit: Nippers is British slang for small children, and also crabs' claws or pincers that nip.

parts.note: scrap is waste material

indicators.note: finally takes the last letter of the word cattle

explanation.surface: Discarded cattle are left to graze.
explanation.walkthrough: 'graze' reads as cattle feeding, but it is a skinned knee.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrape is a minor wound where skin is scuffed off, the same as a graze.

parts.note: to quit is to withdraw or leave

explanation.surface: Settle an account and pull out.
explanation.definitionFit: To acquit a defendant is to declare them not guilty, clearing them of a charge.

clue.text: Pepper baked pie with mint and pinch of origanum

indicators.note: baked suggests ingredients transformed in the oven, so the letters are rearranged
a pinch of means just a little, the first letter of origanum

explanation.surface: A recipe for a baked pie with mint and a pinch of oregano.
explanation.walkthrough: 'baked' rearranges the letters of pie and mint; origanum is another name for oregano.
explanation.definitionFit: A pimiento is a sweet red pepper, the kind used to stuff olives.

indicators.note: holding means the word for time wraps round the other letters

parts.note: eve is a poetic word for evening, a time of day
OK means fair or satisfactory

explanation.surface: A festive season of fairs or wakes, held at a set time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fair' and 'wake' both look like old festivals, but fair is OK and wake is the definition, as in waking a memory.
explanation.definitionFit: To evoke is to call up or arouse a feeling or memory, to awaken it.

parts.note: an ace is an expert
tone means mood or spirit

explanation.surface: A specialist with alcohol or a cleaning fluid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spirit' suggests alcohol to go with the solvent, but it gives TONE.
explanation.definitionFit: Acetone is a colourless liquid used to dissolve paint and nail varnish.

clue.text: Mug, from auction's last reduced lots

indicators.note: last means the final letter of auction's, ignoring the apostrophe s

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

indicators.note: reduced means cut short, so the final letter is removed

parts.note: oodles means lots

explanation.surface: A mug sold from cut-price lots at the end of an auction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mug' looks like a cup, but it means a dupe, and noodle is slang for a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: Noodle is slang for a silly person, and a mug is a gullible fool.

indicators.note: consumed in means swallowed up, so the energy letter sits inside the other word

parts.note: fat means plentiful, as in a fat profit
E is the abbreviation for energy

explanation.surface: Boundless energy is used up in a daring deed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exploit' looks like a verb but is the noun, a great deed.
explanation.definitionFit: A feat is a notable achievement, an exploit.

clue.text: Uncertainty shown by divine about US priest

indicators.note: about means going round, so the word for divine wraps the others

parts.note: to divine is to sense intuitively

explanation.surface: Doubt is felt by a clergyman about an American priest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'divine' looks like a clergyman, but it is a verb meaning sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Suspense is a state of anxious uncertainty about what will happen.
